result:
`bun run typecheck` passes clean and `bun test` is 17/17 green (4 files), and `bunx guren check` reports 0 failures.

I made the excerpt optional and derived it from the body when blank. The derivation rule lives in a new `app/Support/excerpt.ts`: `deriveExcerpt(body)` trims the body, returns it whole when it is ≤140 characters, and otherwise cuts at 140 — backing off to the last whitespace only when characters 140 and 141 are both non-whitespace (falling through to a hard cut at 140 when the opening has no whitespace at all) — then trims trailing whitespace and appends a single `…` (U+2026); `resolveExcerpt(excerpt, body)` prefers a non-blank provided excerpt and falls back to the derived one. In `app/Http/Validators/PostValidator.ts` the `excerpt` field on `PostPayloadSchema` lost its `.min(1)` and became `.optional()` (still trimmed, still capped at 500), leaving the title and body rules untouched so blank ones still 422; `PostController.store()` and `PostController.update()` now pass `excerpt: resolveExcerpt(data.excerpt, data.body)`, so an update that clears the field re-derives from the new body. Both forms (`resources/js/pages/posts/New.tsx`, `Edit.tsx`) label the field "Excerpt (optional)", add a placeholder explaining the fallback, and tolerate an undefined value; `.guren/api-client.gen.ts` was regenerated via `bun run codegen`. New tests cover the rule and the routes: `tests/excerpt.test.ts` asserts both worked examples character-for-character plus the boundary cases, and `tests/PostExcerpt.test.ts` exercises create/update over HTTP (omitted, whitespace-only, and provided excerpts, plus the unchanged title/body validation).
